newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-GARRIDO SURVIVES JITTERS FOR FIRST TOUR WIN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-GARRIDO SURVIVES JITTERS FOR FIRST TOUR WIN.

text.p: Ignacio Garrido survived mid-round jitters to win the rain-affected German Open on Sunday, in the end by a comfortable four strokes.
It was a maiden victory in his fourth year on the European Tour for the 25-year-old Spaniard who is attempting to emulate his father Antonio by winning a place on the Ryder Cup team.
Garrido's one-over-par 72 gave him a 13 under four round total of 271, four ahead of Briton Russell Claydon who moved rapidly up the leader board with the day's best round of 66.
Garrido began the final round five strokes clear of the field but in a nervy spell allowed 22-year-old Briton Brian Davis to close to within two strokes.

But it was Davis, also seeking a first Tour win, who succumbed to the pressure. When he double-bogeyed the 14th, he not only dropped out of the hunt for the 116,000 pounds ($192,000) first prize but at last took the pressure off Garrido.
Briton Mark James, who with Davis had been Garrido's nearest overnight challenger, was a further stroke back on 276.
Davis bogeyed the last to drop back into a group of five on 277 which also included Germany's Bernhard Langer. Defending champion Ian Woosnam tailed away to finish nine shots behind.
Heavy rain delayed the start causing the final round to be revamped into two-tee starts and with players going round in threesomes.

"Today was not easy because it became quite windy after the rain and obviously the pressure was great for me trying for my first victory, especially on the back nine when Brian got up close," said Garrido.
"It's good to be champion and I hope it won't be the last time because I have a long way to go to catch up my father's record."
His father won five times on the European Tour and played in the 1979 Ryder Cup, where he was Severiano Ballesteros's first partner.
Garrido's win moved him up to 13th in the European Ryder Cup table only three off an automatic selection placing.
Should he make captain Ballesteros's team it would be only the second time a son had followed his father into the Ryder Cup team, following Britain's Peter and Percy Alliss.
